18:The bulk of Plaintiffs’ breach claim centers around their argument that TD’s conduct violated the NACHA Rules, which Plaintiffs claim were incorporated into the Account Agreement. See Compl. at ¶ 166-67. In order to address this claim we must first determine whether the NACHA rules were in fact incorporated. In support of this point, Plaintiffs cite to page 16 of the Account Agreement, which states in relevant part:
19:International ACH and Wire Transactions
20:If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved....
21:As TD points out, this provision does not refer to all ACH transactions, but rather only to those initiated from outside of the United States. Motion to Dismiss at 18 (Doc. No. 23). Thus to the extent that an ACH transaction was initiated within the United States, we see nothing in the Account Agreement that would obligate TD to follow the NACHA rules for processing that transaction.

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c001","reasoning_cat1":"A plain claims-made notice; the only softness is 'ERODE THE LIMITS', which the operative Section III.D and Endorsement 6 spell out precisely.","reasoning_cat2":"It says claims must be reported 'DURING THE POLICY PERIOD' while Insuring Agreements I.A/I.B and Section VIII permit reporting during an 'extended reporting period', a modest tension a court could be asked to harmonise.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c002","reasoning_cat1":"A short integration statement listing the documents that constitute the policy; nothing in it carries two meanings.","reasoning_cat2":"It fits the endorsement structure and IX.K (Changes and Assignment); no competing integration or priority-of-documents clause exists.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c003","reasoning_cat1":"The parenthetical is garbled ('Item. 2.a and/or litem, 3.a., above., whichever is earlier') and '100 % minimum-earned' as a percentage figure is stated oddly.","reasoning_cat2":"IX.A.3 says the 'premium percentage identified in Item 5.' is the minimum earned premium and then provides for pro rata earning of 'remaining unearned premium' and a refund, which cannot be reconciled with a 100% minimum-earned premium.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c004","reasoning_cat1":"Identical to the Declarations notice; standard claims-made language with no term needing construction beyond OCR noise ('WHAT 1S').","reasoning_cat2":"Same tension with I.A/I.B and Section VIII extended reporting period reporting windows as the Declarations notice.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c005","reasoning_cat1":"A simple interpretive convention that quoted words are defined in Section V.","reasoning_cat2":"Several quoted terms are in fact undefined ('covered operations' in Endorsement 6.I.E/F, 'loss' in Endorsement 6.IV.F), so the convention does not hold across the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c006","reasoning_cat1":"Boilerplate consideration and reliance clause; nothing to construe on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with IX.F Representations and the Fraud or Misrepresentation exclusion; no conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c007","reasoning_cat1":"A lead-in conditioning coverage on the Declarations identifying the coverage; plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplemental Coverages added by Endorsements 3, 4 and 13 are not 'identified on the Declarations', so the lead-in sits awkwardly with them even though Item 4 refers to Supplemental Coverages.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c008","reasoning_cat1":"'first commence, in their entirety, during the policy period' is a demanding and contestable trigger for a continuing condition, and 'arising out of' is broad.","reasoning_cat2":"This subsection is deleted and replaced twice, by Endorsement 5.II (retroactive-date version) and Endorsement 10.I (transportation version), which are inconsistent with each other and leave the operative Coverage A text uncertain.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c009","reasoning_cat1":"Contains the typo 'nolicy period' and pairs 'first commenced, in whole or part, prior to the policy period' with a requirement that discovery occur during the period.","reasoning_cat2":"Read with Coverage A (c008) the two coverages divide conditions by commencement date; the Endorsement 5 retroactive-date rewrite of Coverage A blurs that division for scheduled locations.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c010","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed and internally consistent SIR attachment language; 'satisfactory evidence' is the only soft term.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with V.AA, III.D and IX.D (bankruptcy does not relieve the SIR obligation); no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c011","reasoning_cat1":"A mechanical per-condition limit keyed to Item 2.b.; nothing ambiguous except the familiar 'same, continuous, repeated, or related' aggregation phrase.","reasoning_cat2":"Endorsement 6.I deletes and replaces this subsection, dropping 'legal defense expense' from it, so the base text no longer operates.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c012","reasoning_cat1":"Straightforward aggregate limit provision keyed to Item 2.c.","reasoning_cat2":"Item 2.c is $9,000,000 while Item 4's Total Policy Aggregate is $7,000,000, and this subsection is also replaced by Endorsement 6.I.D — a genuine numerical incoherence.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c013","reasoning_cat1":"Plain per-condition limit for Coverage B keyed to Item 3.b.","reasoning_cat2":"Endorsement 6.I.E deletes and replaces it with text adding the undefined qualifier 'resulting from covered operations', which narrows it in a way the base policy nowhere supports.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c014","reasoning_cat1":"Plain aggregate limit for Coverage B keyed to Item 3.c.","reasoning_cat2":"Replaced by Endorsement 6.I.F, which introduces the undefined term 'covered operations'; the base and endorsed versions cover different ground.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.34},

{"clause_id":"c069","reasoning_cat1":"'other conveyance' after a list of automobile, aircraft, watercraft and railcar is a classic ejusdem generis catch-all.","reasoning_cat2":"Endorsement 10.III deletes and replaces this exclusion, and the carve-back for 'contingent transportation' refers to a definition Endorsement 10.II has already deleted.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.35},

{"clause_id":"c071","reasoning_cat1":"'must see it that the Insurer receives written notice ... as soon as practicable' is mandatory, but the content requirements are only what notice 'should include' — a permissive/mandatory mismatch within one clause.","reasoning_cat2":"The insuring agreements require written reporting 'during the policy period', which is a hard deadline that sits against this 'as soon as practicable' standard.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c072","reasoning_cat1":"The numbering is broken (items 3 and 4 lost their numerals), but the duties themselves are conventional and clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with VII.C, IX.E (subrogation cooperation) and IX.C.2's compliance condition.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.13},

{"clause_id":"c074","reasoning_cat1":"'make every attempt to mitigate' and 'in the sole judgment of the insurer' are both soft, and the two standards operate on the same facts.","reasoning_cat2":"'Sole judgment' sits against IX.M's requirement that consent not be unreasonably withheld, and deemed-incurred remediation costs interact with VII.C's consent bar.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c075","reasoning_cat1":"Short and, read alone, clear as to entitlement.","reasoning_cat2":"It ties the ERP to cancellation 'as described in Subsection A., Paragraph 1. of Section IX.', which is cancellation by the first named insured only, apparently denying an ERP after insurer cancellation under Paragraph 2 — a real cross-reference problem.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.39},

{"clause_id":"c078","reasoning_cat1":"'not more than two hundred percent (200%) of the full premium' fixes a ceiling but not the actual price, leaving the charge indeterminate.","reasoning_cat2":"Endorsement 7 replaces this with a thirty-three month version; the 34/33-month difference and the 60/90-day basic period must be read together.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.28},

{"clause_id":"c083","reasoning_cat1":"The waterfall is oddly drafted: recovery accrues 'first to the insureds to the extent of any payments in excess of the limit of coverage', then the Insurer, then the insured for the SIR — the first tier's meaning is not obvious.","reasoning_cat2":"It coordinates with the SIR provisions in II.A and IX.D without contradiction.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c084","reasoning_cat1":"Converting Application statements into 'warranties' is consequential but stated plainly.","reasoning_cat2":"The Fraud or Misrepresentation exclusion (VI.G) and cancellation condition 2.b. limit misrepresentation consequences to the culpable insured, whereas a warranty theory would void coverage generally.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.30},

{"clause_id":"c086","reasoning_cat1":"Standard excess-of-other-insurance clause with a single carve-out; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with IX.D's non-drop-down sentence; no conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c087","reasoning_cat1":"'the exclusive jurisdiction of the State of New York' is genuinely ambiguous — it names a sovereign rather than a court, so whether it means New York state courts only or any court sitting in New York is contestable, and the removal-preservation sentence pulls the other way.","reasoning_cat2":"It squarely conflicts with the Service of Suit Endorsement (No. 15), under which the company 'will submit to the jurisdiction of any court of competent jurisdiction' at the insured's request, and with IX.C's suit conditions.","prob_cat1":0.68,"prob_cat2":0.74},
{"clause_id":"c088","reasoning_cat1":"A comprehensive and conventional New York choice-of-law clause; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits with the venue clause and the Iowa Surplus Lines notification, and any dispute about the venue clause will inevitably raise which law construes it.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c089","reasoning_cat1":"Anti-waiver and anti-assignment in one paragraph; 'except as provided by endorsement and attached to this Policy' is slightly garbled but the sense is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Declarations' integration statement and with the Service of Suit endorsement's non-variation sentence.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c090","reasoning_cat1":"A short, standard headings clause.","reasoning_cat2":"Other operative provisions identify exclusions purely by heading (IX.G refers to 'the Known Conditions Exclusion', 'the Material Change in Risk Exclusion'), so a rule that headings 'do not constitute any part of the terms' is in tension with the way the policy actually cross-refers.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.35},
{"clause_id":"c091","reasoning_cat1":"'shall not be unreasonably withheld, delayed, conditioned, or denied' is a familiar standard applied globally.","reasoning_cat2":"It contradicts provisions that give the Insurer unqualified discretion — VI.H's approval 'at its sole discretion' and VII.D's 'sole judgment of the insurer'.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c092","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line schedule adding a single named insured; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with V.S and IX.G; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c093","reasoning_cat1":"'solely with respect to their vicarious liability arising out of any named insured's direct liability' is a notoriously tricky formulation, and the sentence has no closing punctuation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with V.A's rule that an additional insured has only the rights specified by endorsement; no conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c094","reasoning_cat1":"'in excess of the Deductible Period' measures a loss against a period of time rather than a dollar amount, an awkward formulation, and 'directly attributable' is a soft causal test.","reasoning_cat2":"The $5,000,000 sublimit is stated to be subject to the Declarations limits, but the Total Policy Aggregate is only $7,000,000 and business interruption loss is not among the categories Item 4 aggregates.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c095","reasoning_cat1":"'Net profit or loss ... that would have been realized' is inherently counterfactual, and the payroll carve-out list is specific.","reasoning_cat2":"Coordinates with 'business interruption', 'rental income' and IV.B; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c096","reasoning_cat1":"'necessary partial or complete suspension' is broad — 'necessary' and 'partial' both admit argument about slowdowns short of shutdown.","reasoning_cat2":"Read with 'period of interruption' and IV.A/IV.B the mechanism is coherent.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c097","reasoning_cat1":"A three-item definitional list; the missing closing quotation mark on 'Extra expense' is cosmetic.","reasoning_cat2":"Each component is separately defined in the same endorsement; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c098","reasoning_cat1":"Ties business interruption coverage to conditions covered 'for remediation costs resulting from the first-party discovery', a narrow and somewhat convoluted qualifier.","reasoning_cat2":"Because Endorsement 12 narrows 'pollution condition' and adds exclusions, the set of 'covered pollution conditions' shifts with those endorsements, but no direct contradiction appears.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c099","reasoning_cat1":"The lead-in is ungrammatical ('where a covered pollution condition causes a delay ... any of the following expenses incurred shall be afforded coverage') and item 3 lost its numeral.","reasoning_cat2":"Only applies to 'a covered location under development', which none of the scheduled egg-production sites obviously is; no conflict, just limited reach.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c100","reasoning_cat1":"'necessary to avoid or mitigate' plus 'must be incurred to actually minimize' sets a double and somewhat circular test.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with VII.D's mitigation duty and with 'business income'; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.15}
]}
